data.user_prompt: Is Next.js with Sanity a good stack for a consultant website?

sections.text:
Yes — **Next.js + Sanity is a strong stack for a consultant website** if you want a fast, SEO-friendly site with easy content editing and room to grow into case studies, blog posts, landing pages, and reusable content sections.[1][10][15]

Why it fits well:

- **Great for marketing and SEO:** Next.js is commonly used for content-driven sites and supports modern rendering patterns, while Sanity provides structured content that works well for SEO fields and dynamic content delivery.[1][4][7]
- **Easy for non-developers to edit:** Sanity offers a customizable editing environment, real-time collaboration, previews, and content modeling that lets you manage services, testimonials, FAQs, and case studies without changing code.[1][7][17]
- **Flexible for consultant-style sites:** Sanity’s schema-based content model is a good fit when your site needs more than a simple brochure layout, such as author bios, project pages, reusable call-to-action blocks, and related content.[3][7][15]
- **Efficient development workflow:** Next.js handles rendering and routing, while Sanity acts as the content backend; this split is explicitly recommended in Sanity’s Next.js documentation and is designed for modern React patterns.[1][17][20]

A few tradeoffs to consider:

- **More setup than a plain static site:** This stack gives you more power, but it also introduces more moving parts than using a simple website builder or a lightweight static site generator.[2][14]
- **Best when content will change often:** If your consultant site is just a few fixed pages and rarely updated, the stack may be more than you need.[2][15]
- **Content modeling matters:** Sanity is especially useful when you want structured content, but you need to define that structure up front.[2][7][12]

A practical rule:

- Choose **Next.js + Sanity** if you want a polished personal or consulting site with blog posts, service pages, landing pages, testimonials, and easy future expansion.[1][15][18]
- Choose something simpler if you only need a very small brochure site with minimal updates.[2][14]

If you want, I can also recommend the **best folder setup** for a consultant site using Next.js + Sanity, or help you decide between this stack and a simpler alternative.
